original_content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Particle and the Origin
original_content.problem:
A car accelerates from rest at the origin with an acceleration of $(3i-4j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $2i\,\text{m/s}.$ Find the distance from the car to the origin$(|r|)$ after $4$ seconds.

$\,|r|=$ 
{{field-1}}
$\text{m}$
original_content.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=2i,\,a=3i-4j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the car after $t=4\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(2i)(4)+\frac{1}{2}(3i-4j)(4)^{2} \\  & =8i+8(3i-4j) \\  & =8i+24i-32j \\  & =(32i-32j)\,\text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the car to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|32i-32j| \\  & =\sqrt{(32)^{2}+(-32)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1024+1024} \\  & =\sqrt{2048} \\  & =32\sqrt{2}\,\text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$

corrected_content.problem:
A car accelerates from the origin with an acceleration of $(3i-4j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $2i\,\text{m/s}.$ Find the distance from the car to the origin$(|r|)$ after $4$ seconds.

$\,|r|=$ 
{{field-1}}
$\text{m}$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
With constant acceleration, the position is

$$
\mathbf r(t)=\mathbf r_0+\mathbf u t+\tfrac12\mathbf a t^2.
$$

Here $\mathbf r_0=\mathbf0$, $\mathbf u=2\mathbf i\,\mathrm{m/s}$, and $\mathbf a=(3\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. At $t=4\,\mathrm{s}$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf r(4)&=\mathbf0+(2\mathbf i)(4)+\tfrac12(3\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)(4^2)\\
&=8\mathbf i+24\mathbf i-32\mathbf j\\
&=(32\mathbf i-32\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m.
\end{aligned}
$$

The distance to the origin is therefore

$$
|\mathbf r(4)|=\sqrt{32^2+(-32)^2}=\sqrt{2048}=\boxed{32\sqrt2\,\mathrm m}.
$$
